title: How do they compare? 比一比
description: Lesson 110 is a picture lesson about comparatives and superlatives of quantity and quality. Eight groups of three pictures (I–Z) compare things like chocolate, mistakes, cars and restaurants. The lesson uses much/many, little/few, more/most, less/least, fewer/fewest, better/best and worse/worst, followed by written exercises, workbook practice and a grammar workbook section comparing people's possessions and exam results.
answer_note: Listening, written exercises A–D are model answers (suggested). Workbook A and B are from the workbook answer key (source-key). Grammar I and II are from the grammar workbook answer key (source-key). Grammar source audit: see reports/grammar-source-audit.json; source section order, complete prompts and answers restored.

lesson.text:
Have you got any chocolate?
I haven't got much.
I've got more than you have.

Have you got any chocolate?
I've got very little.
I've got less than you have.

Have you made any mistakes?
I haven't made many.
I've made more than you have.

Have you made any mistakes?
I've made very few.
I've made fewer than you have.

You must see my new car.
It's very good.
This one's the best I've ever seen.

You mustn't go to that restaurant.
It's very bad.
This one's the worst I've ever seen.
